title: Word 15 — On the Christian Upbringing of Children
attribution_note: Word 15 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: This is a word that the Holy Spirit speaks through the apostle to parents, exhorting them to bring up their children as befits Christians: *“Bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.”* All Christians were renewed in holy Baptism to a new, holy, and Christian life, and promised to serve God in faith and truth, and so to please Him. But so that the baptized do not fall into corruption and come to a state of ruin, and so that it does not happen to them according to the true proverb — *“The dog returns to its own vomit, and the washed sow to wallowing in the mire”* [2 Peter 2:22] — parents must without fail forestall this ruin by the good upbringing of their children while they are still small and young. For we see with grief and sighing that many children fall into corruption in their youth. This happens to them through the negligence of their parents. Many parents teach their children the arts and skills that serve this temporal life; some take pains to teach them foreign languages, and spend no small money on this, but take no care for Christian instruction, and make no effort to teach their children to live as Christians. Such parents bring their children into being for temporal life, but shut the doors to eternal life against them.

sections.heading: The judgment of St John Chrysostom

pairs.en: St John Chrysostom, reflecting on parents who neglect the good upbringing of their children, and on the calamity of poorly raised children, says: “Parents who neglect to raise their children as Christians are more lawless than murderers of children. For murderers separate only the body from the soul, but these cast both soul and body into the fire of Gehenna. Bodily death, by the law of nature, can in no way be avoided, but the death of the soul could be avoided, were it not that the negligence of parents is to blame for it. Moreover, the coming resurrection can at once undo bodily death, but nothing can restore the ruin of a soul” [Homily 5 Against the Opponents of the Monastic Life]. Therefore, parents, hear the word of the Lord: *“Bring up your children in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.”*

sections.heading: The gardener and the young tree

pairs.en: Bind their hearts to the fear of God, so that they are not shaken by satanic schemes and do not abandon piety, and cut away the passions growing up in them, lest these passions grow and take hold of them, and so put to death the inner new man born in holy Baptism. For we see that as children grow, sinful passions appear and grow along with them, like useless shoots on a tree. Therefore, so that these lawless shoots do not grow up, and do not harm or destroy the person washed, sanctified, and justified in holy Baptism, they must without fail be cut away by the Lord's instruction and teaching. Cut away, then, beloved, such shoots from your children, and *“bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.”* As soon as they begin to understand even a little, and to know good from evil, begin your own work and teach them.

6) Set before them their end — death, the judgment of Christ, eternal life, and eternal torment — so that in this way the fear of God may take root in them, and they may guard themselves from every evil.

Pour all this, and more besides, like milk into their young hearts, that they may grow up in piety. They call you their parents — be, then, true parents. You gave them birth according to the flesh — give them birth also according to the spirit. You brought them into temporal life — bring them to birth also for eternal life.

sections.heading: The reckoning at the Last Judgment

pairs.en: Beloved Christians! You and your children alike will appear at the dread Judgment of Christ, and you will give account for them before the righteous Judge. He will not ask you whether you taught your children the arts, whether you taught them to speak French, German, or Italian, but whether you taught them to live as Christians. Young children heed their parents' actions far more than their instruction. Therefore, if you want your children to be pious and good, be pious and good yourselves, and show yourselves to them as an example, and so *“bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.”* Then both your children and you will receive eternal salvation in Christ Jesus our Lord. Amen.
